source_text: Digo, "Disfrutemos, disfrutemos porque en cualquier momento vamos a estar tomando mate en una cocinita de nuevo."
target_text: I say, "Let's enjoy, let's enjoy because at any moment we are going to be drinking mate in a little kitchen again."
annotation_notes: Repeated forms must link to different target occurrences.

source_text: Mm, decía que vamos a hablar sobre recuerdos usando el pasado.
target_text: Mm, I was saying that we are going to talk about memories using the past.
annotation_notes: A prior coarse group caused the whole English tail to flash.

source_text: Creo que más que el mexicano no sepa decir que no, el mexicano no sabe aceptar un no como respuesta.
target_text: I think that more than the Mexican not knowing how to say no, the Mexican does not know how to accept a no as an answer.
annotation_notes: Reported browser miss around no sepa decir que no.

source_text: Escuchen, yo les voy a contar la rutina, eh, y esto va a ser así.
target_text: Listen, I am going to tell you the routine, uh, and this is going to be like this.
annotation_notes: Reported browser case with omitted middle and tail links.

source_text: ¿Por qué no funciona?
target_text: Why isn't it working?
annotation_notes: Noncontiguous/many-to-many English question structure.

source_text: Este parking está al lado de la carretera que no me importa.
target_text: This parking is next to the road, which I don't mind.
annotation_notes: The relative clause should not become one whole-sentence group.

source_text: A ver, vamos a pensar, por ejemplo, ¿cuál es tu excusa por excelencia?
target_text: Let's see, let's think, for example, what is your excuse par excellence?
annotation_notes: Known browser success retained as a contrast case.

source_text: Tienen que decir: cuidado, que no se vea Juan.
target_text: You have to say: be careful that Juan isn't seen.
annotation_notes: The original joint schema failed validation on this caption.

source_text: Se me olvidó por completo llamarla ayer.
target_text: I completely forgot to call her yesterday.
annotation_notes: Spanish clitics and adverbial phrase reorder.

source_text: Aunque no venga Ana, no vamos a cancelar la reunión 🙂.
target_text: Even if Ana doesn't come, we aren't going to cancel the meeting 🙂.
annotation_notes: Emoji remains a nonlexical gap outside the graph.

source_text: Ich rufe dich morgen wieder an.
target_text: I'll call you again tomorrow.
annotation_notes: The two parts of anrufen both link to call.

source_text: Weil er den Zug verpasst hat, kommt er später.
target_text: Because he missed the train, he is coming later.
annotation_notes: Subordinate-clause verb order differs strongly.

source_text: Der Fahrkartenautomat funktioniert heute nicht.
target_text: The ticket machine isn't working today.
annotation_notes: Compound decomposition and contracted negation.

source_text: Sie hat das Licht ausgemacht, bevor sie gegangen ist.
target_text: She turned off the light before she left.
annotation_notes: Past participles and auxiliaries collapse in English.

source_text: Warum hörst du mir nicht zu?
target_text: Why aren't you listening to me?
annotation_notes: Question auxiliary yields discontinuous links.

source_text: Das hätte ich nicht sagen sollen.
target_text: I shouldn't have said that.
annotation_notes: Modal and perfect auxiliaries redistribute.

source_text: Wenn du Zeit hast, können wir darüber sprechen.
target_text: If you have time, we can talk about it.
annotation_notes: darüber expands into a discontinuous semantic phrase.

source_text: Nein, nein, so war das nicht gemeint.
target_text: No, no, that wasn't how it was meant.
annotation_notes: Repeated nein occurrences must remain distinct.

source_text: Die Entscheidung, die wir getroffen haben, war schwierig.
target_text: The decision we made was difficult.
annotation_notes: English may omit the relative pronoun.

source_text: Mach dir keine Sorgen — das kriegen wir hin 🙂.
target_text: Don't worry — we'll manage it 🙂.
annotation_notes: Two German idioms require many-to-many links.

source_text: Эту книгу я вчера наконец дочитал.
target_text: I finally finished reading this book yesterday.
annotation_notes: Case marking permits strong reordering.

source_text: Она врач, а её брат учитель.
target_text: She is a doctor, and her brother is a teacher.
annotation_notes: English supplies two absent present-tense copulas.

source_text: Я не успел ему перезвонить.
target_text: I didn't manage to call him back.
annotation_notes: Prefix semantics appears as English back.

source_text: Что же я тогда сделал не так?
target_text: What did I do wrong then?
annotation_notes: же is pragmatically unaligned; English auxiliary splits from verb.

source_text: Мне эта идея совсем не нравится.
target_text: I don't like this idea at all.
annotation_notes: Russian experiencer case becomes English subject.

source_text: Письмо было написано Анной вчера.
target_text: The letter was written by Anna yesterday.
annotation_notes: Instrumental agent expands into by plus name.

source_text: Если бы ты позвонил раньше, мы бы успели.
target_text: If you had called earlier, we would have made it.
annotation_notes: Two бы occurrences contribute to different English auxiliaries.

source_text: Он всё говорил и говорил об одном и том же.
target_text: He kept talking and talking about the same thing.
annotation_notes: Repeated verb occurrences remain distinct.

source_text: Новой машины у нас пока нет.
target_text: We don't have a new car yet.
annotation_notes: Existential negation changes argument structure.

source_text: Маша сказала: «Я сама это сделаю» 🙂.
target_text: Masha said, ‘I'll do it myself’ 🙂.
annotation_notes: Russian synthetic future maps to contracted English auxiliary and verb.

source_text: 我把那本书看完了。
target_text: I finished reading that book.
annotation_notes: 把 is unaligned; reviewed no-space segmentation is supplied.

source_text: 这件事不是我做的。
target_text: I wasn't the one who did this.
annotation_notes: Chinese shi-de cleft becomes an English relative construction.

source_text: 他昨天给我打了两个电话。
target_text: He called me twice yesterday.
annotation_notes: 打电话 collapses to called; quantity becomes twice.

source_text: 门被风吹开了。
target_text: The door was blown open by the wind.
annotation_notes: 被 corresponds to passive auxiliary and by.

source_text: 你怎么还没吃饭？
target_text: How come you still haven't eaten?
annotation_notes: 怎么 becomes two English words.

source_text: 我不是不想去，只是没有时间。
target_text: It's not that I don't want to go; I just don't have time.
annotation_notes: Two negative markers map to different target occurrences.

source_text: 老师让学生把手机关掉。
target_text: The teacher made the students turn off their phones.
annotation_notes: 关掉 maps to turn off; 把 is unaligned.

source_text: 那个人我以前见过两次。
target_text: I've seen that person twice before.
annotation_notes: Fronted topic reorders after the English verb.

source_text: 虽然下雨，他还是出门了。
target_text: Although it was raining, he still went out.
annotation_notes: Weather subject and auxiliary are supplied in English.

source_text: 别急，慢慢来 🙂。
target_text: Don't rush; take your time 🙂.
annotation_notes: Second clause is idiomatic and many-to-many.

source_text: 私は昨日その本を読み終えました。
target_text: I finished reading that book yesterday.
annotation_notes: Particles are unaligned; 読み終える splits semantically.

source_text: この写真を撮った人を知っていますか。
target_text: Do you know the person who took this photo?
annotation_notes: Japanese relative clause precedes its head.

source_text: 彼はコーヒーを三杯も飲んだ。
target_text: He drank as many as three cups of coffee.
annotation_notes: も contributes the as-many-as construction.

source_text: 雨に降られて、服が濡れてしまった。
target_text: I got caught in the rain, and my clothes ended up wet.
annotation_notes: English supplies experiencer and possessive.

source_text: どうしてまだ来ていないの？
target_text: Why haven't you come yet?
annotation_notes: English supplies you; final の marks the question.

source_text: 彼にもう一度説明してもらいました。
target_text: I had him explain it to me once more.
annotation_notes: もらう changes the argument structure.

source_text: 鍵をなくしたと思って焦りました。
target_text: I panicked because I thought I had lost my key.
annotation_notes: English repeats I for three omitted subjects.

source_text: いいえ、いいえ、そういう意味ではありません。
target_text: No, no, that's not what I mean.
annotation_notes: Repeated responses and discontinuous negation.

source_text: 駅に着いたら電話してください。
target_text: Please call me when you arrive at the station.
annotation_notes: English supplies you and me.

source_text: まあ、できることはできるけどね 🙂。
target_text: Well, I can do it, technically, but you know 🙂.
annotation_notes: Repeated できる occurrences share English meaning but stay distinct.
